review.notes:
Chain starts at v1 (LCGX-EN217, 2011-10-04), which the baseline implements exactly (ratio 1.0). v0 (SOVR-EN099, 2009-11-17) -> v1 is the PSCT formalisation of the same mandatory Trigger Effects, so the Edison-era printing (v0, in force from 2009-11-17) behaves as the baseline implements. The 'Once per turn' wording added at v2 has no script counterpart - both scripts already apply SetCountLimit(1) to the End Phase pay-500-or-destroy maintenance - so the recorded behavioural difference is the Trigger-to-continuous and targeting change. Upstream also ships 511000306 'Clear World (VG)', the video-game version with materially different text ('You cannot activate Spell Cards'; 'Once per turn, during your turn: Destroy 1 monster you control'; DARK stops all attacks rather than only at 2+ monsters) - not a TCG historical version, excluded. Remaining modern-only code (the fid / STATUS_COPYING_EFFECT guards and the EFFECT_TYPE_SINGLE marker effect) is upstream robustness for effect-copying, not an erratum. Card data identical between 33900658 and 33900648.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Clear World). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [event] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of Maze of the Master (MZTM-EN098), the first printing carrying the errata'd text

event.historical_text: During each of your End Phases, pay 500 Life Points or destroy this card. Each player receives effects, depending on the monster Attributes they control. ● LIGHT: Play with your hand revealed at all times. ● DARK: If you control 2 or more monsters, you cannot declare an attack. ● EARTH: During your Standby Phase: Target 1 face-up Defense Position monster you control; destroy that target. ● WATER: During your End Phase: Discard 1 card. ● FIRE: During your End Phase: Take 1000 damage. ● WIND: You must pay 500 Life Points to activate a Spell Card.
event.modern_text: Once per turn, during your End Phase, pay 500 LP or destroy this card. Each player receives effects, depending on the monster Attributes they control.● LIGHT: Play with your hand revealed at all times.● DARK: If you control 2 or more monsters, you cannot declare an attack.● EARTH: During your Standby Phase, destroy 1 face-up Defense Position monster you control.● WATER: During your End Phase, discard 1 card.● FIRE: During your End Phase, take 1000 damage.● WIND: You must pay 500 LP to activate a Spell Card.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the EARTH, WATER and FIRE penalties stopped being Trigger Effects that start a Chain. The historical script registers all three as EFFECT_TYPE_FIELD+EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_F with EFFECT_FLAG_EVENT_PLAYER - mandatory triggers that form a chain link and can be responded to or negated - and gives the EARTH one EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET plus a SetTarget(s.destg) that targets the Defense Position monster at activation; the modern script registers the same three as EFFECT_TYPE_FIELD+EFFECT_TYPE_CONTINUOUS with no target step, so nothing is targeted and nothing can be chained to. The printed text tracks it: v1's 'During your Standby Phase: Target 1 face-up Defense Position monster you control; destroy that target' becomes v2's 'During your Standby Phase, destroy 1 face-up Defense Position monster you control', and the maintenance clause gains 'Once per turn'.

rulings_check.difference: Era: the EARTH, WATER and FIRE penalties are Trigger Effects that each start their own Chain (so they can be responded to or negated, and resolve without effect if the player is unaffected); modern: continuous effects that start no Chain. Era: the EARTH penalty targets the Defense Position monster when it is put on the Chain ('Target 1 face-up Defense Position monster you control'); modern: no target, the monster is chosen on resolution.
